claim.text: Kesta-9 produced 17 detectable radio pulses on observation night 6.
claim.quantity_definition: Observation night 6 is the interval 20:00 to 04:00 UTC beginning 20 June 2031. A detectable pulse is a burst whose peak signal-to-noise ratio is at least 8 in the 1.40-1.43 GHz band; bursts separated by at least 50 ms count separately. Every observer applies this identical rule to its own recording of the full interval.

shared_factors.factor: Same target emission on the same night (the shared subject)
shared_factors.note: All four observe the same physical pulse train.
All apply the same published rule; the rule is the definition of the quantity, so a flaw in it is common.
Sites are geographically separate, but strong interference could affect several receivers.
All four receivers are the same sensitivity class; no root has a sensitivity advantage.

independence_assessment: Four separate receivers at separate sites, run by separate teams, each count pulses in their own recording using one standardized rule and equal-class sensitivity. No root reads another's output. Disjoint recording ids are not by themselves the basis for independence. Residual correlation: shared counting rule and possible common interference. Human confirmation pending.
